author: Dr Ben Miles
description:
Scientists at the University of Texas at Austin have developed a jacket that harvests moisture from the air and converts it into drinkable water, producing up to 900 milliliters daily depending on humidity. A related technology uses biomass hydrogels and solar heating to yield as much as 1.3 liters per day, offering new solutions for water scarcity in remote or arid environments.
